sections.markdown:
## C — Circular and arrow signals, right turn on red, combination signals, dark or broken signals, flashing signals, flashing yellow arrows, ramp meters and hybrid beacons (North Carolina)
Knowledge domain: what each North Carolina traffic signal display requires of a driver, including circular and arrow signals, turning right on red, combination signal heads, malfunctioning signals, flashing red and yellow, the flashing yellow arrow, freeway ramp meters and pedestrian or emergency hybrid beacons.

FACT_ID: sec14-F01 | anchor: A01
Traffic signals control both vehicles and pedestrians at some intersections and at some mid-block crosswalks. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec14-F02 | anchor: A01
A circular green light lets you go straight or turn with caution, but turning drivers must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec14-F03 | anchor: A01
A circular yellow light warns that red is coming: stop unless you are too close to stop safely, in which case continue carefully through. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec14-F04 | anchor: A01
Never speed up on a yellow light to try to get through before it turns red. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec14-F05 | anchor: A01
A steady circular red means stop, and you may then turn right after a complete stop unless a NO TURN ON RED sign is posted. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec14-F06 | anchor: A01
A driver turning right on red must yield to other traffic and to pedestrians in the intersection or starting to cross nearby in front of the stopped traffic. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec14-F07 | anchor: A01
Failing to yield to such a pedestrian while turning right on red carries a penalty of at least $100 and no more than $500. [A01]
Why it matters: dynamic fact; penalty amounts are set by law and can change.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec14-F08 | anchor: A01
A green arrow gives a protected movement, allowing you to enter the intersection carefully in the direction the arrow points. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec14-F09 | anchor: A01
When a U-turn and an opposing right turn both have green arrows at once, the U-turning driver yields to the right-turning driver. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec14-F10 | anchor: A01
A red arrow means drivers turning in that direction must stop. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec14-F11 | anchor: A01
A yellow arrow warns that the protected green arrow is ending and will change to a circular green, a circular red or a red arrow. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec14-F12 | anchor: A02
Some signals combine protected arrows with unprotected circular lights; when no arrow is lit, circular lights control both through and turning traffic. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec14-F13 | anchor: A02
When arrows and circular lights show together, the arrows control turning traffic and the circular lights control through traffic. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec14-F14 | anchor: A02
At a signal that is dark or malfunctioning, treat the intersection as if every approach had a stop sign. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec14-F15 | anchor: A02
The all-way-stop rule for a broken signal does not apply when an officer or other authorized person directs traffic or another control device is working. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec14-F16 | anchor: A02
A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign: stop and wait until you can enter without interfering with approaching traffic. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec14-F17 | anchor: A02
A flashing yellow light means the same as a warning sign: slow down and go on with caution. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec14-F18 | anchor: A02
A flashing yellow arrow permits the turn shown, but you must first yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec14-F19 | anchor: A02
On a flashing yellow arrow signal head, a solid red arrow means stop with no turn allowed, and a solid yellow arrow means get ready to stop. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec14-F20 | anchor: A02
A solid green arrow on that head allows the turn without yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians, though you still proceed with caution. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec14-F21 | anchor: A02
Signal heads for right turns may show a steady circular red instead of a red arrow. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec14-F22 | anchor: A03
A ramp meter controls traffic entering a freeway from an interchange entrance ramp. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec14-F23 | anchor: A03
At a ramp meter, steady red means stop and wait, and steady green means go down the ramp and merge onto the freeway. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec14-F24 | anchor: A03
If a ramp meter is dark, showing neither red nor green, you may continue without stopping and merge or yield as conditions allow. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec14-F25 | anchor: A03
Hybrid beacons can control traffic at mid-block crosswalks and at the entrances of emergency response facilities, and stay dark until a pedestrian or responder activates them. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec14-F26 | anchor: A03
Once activated, a hybrid beacon flashes yellow, then shows steady yellow and then steady red so moving vehicles can stop safely. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec14-F27 | anchor: A03
While a hybrid beacon shows steady red, vehicles stay stopped as pedestrians cross or emergency vehicles leave their station. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec14-F28 | anchor: A03
When the hybrid beacon switches to flashing red, stay stopped until the pedestrians or emergency vehicles have cleared; then, after a full stop, you may proceed while it still flashes. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec14-F29 | anchor: A03
After its cycle, a hybrid beacon goes dark again until the next activation. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0084]

Misconceptions: yellow does not mean speed up; a dark signal is not a free pass but an all-way stop; a flashing yellow arrow allows the turn only after yielding; right on red requires a full stop first and is barred where signed; a dark ramp meter means merge normally, not stop; a flashing red hybrid beacon still requires waiting until the crossing is clear.
Mnemonics: green go with care, yellow stop if you safely can, red stop; arrows protect, circles permit; flashing red equals stop sign, flashing yellow equals warning sign; dark signal, treat as all-way stop.
Glossary: protected turn means a turn on a green arrow with opposing traffic held; unprotected turn means a turn on a circular green or flashing yellow arrow that requires yielding; ramp meter means a signal that controls entry from an entrance ramp onto a freeway; hybrid beacon means a signal that stays dark until a pedestrian or responder activates it; combination signal means a head showing both arrows and circular lights.
Dynamic facts: the penalty range for failing to yield to a pedestrian on a right turn on red is set by statute and is flagged as dynamic.
